reviews.film: Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me
reviews.review:
whats trauma? trauma is something not easily contextualized. not easily processed. trauma is horrible and stays with you till the day you die. trauma is scary and messes with you in ways you can't easily decipher

fire walk with me is a film that does wonders to cement twin peaks as one of the best tv series because it's able to re-contextualize everything twin peaks and its creators intend and mean

twin peaks has always been on the surface about defrauding the idea of a quaint american town - going way beyond what is normal to really show us the horrible reality that lies beneath the happy exterior

throughout the show, there is constant talk of laura palmer and she quickly becomes this symbol of "purity that's been lost" amongst the people of twin peaks. us as viewers are also bought into this as one character after the other talks so highly of laura and tell us how much everyone is shook by her passing. people grieve, the police gets active but the reality remains far from it. throughout the show we realize the sheer exterior everyone puts up while everyone is busy cheating with other people, tolerating convicted felons and serial assaulters in the same vein as the victim, drug trafficking and probing underage children into prostitution. yet, since we spend so much time with these people, we too are unable to objectively judge these characters for who they are and get wrapped up in their drama and problems. we too forgive all the problems because well yes firstly its a show but largely because its comforting. its comforting to think of this as a town with its small problems but major trouble beginning with the loss of their purity symbol, their homecoming queen.

fire walk with me is a devastating blow to the gut as you see the pain laura had to endure on a daily basis until it hammers home to us the horrible fact that we had been comfortable thinking we knew someone we have never met or seen, comfortable projecting this image for it was convenient and easier. episodes through episodes, her smiling photo hides a truth so unbearable that its quite literally easier to detach it from our head.

its heartbreaking to realize that bob isn't some scary monster from some other world that hijacks people but something laura had created in her head to shield her from the fact that her father has been sexually abusing her since she was a little child. her mother smoking to her death is not because she is reckless but her only way to cope up with this. it's easier to imagine things - it's easier to forget things - it's easier to form up apparitions.

leland himself isn't free from this cycle. a throwaway line from the show about him recalling bob from near a childhood home reveals him having to encounter bob as he was too sexually abused as a child.

laura isnt the hedonistic person we see because of her "dark side" - rather, her dark side was manufactured by everyone around her. everyone wanting the convenience of loving her 'pure self', everyone wanting to abuse her young helpless self.

whats bob, really? thats an important question. bob exists inside all of us. bob haunts us or possesses us. bob drives us to do horrible things or bob chases us with his horrors. whether its dale cooper falling for his teammates wife behind his back or ed being happy that his wife's mental state deteriorates just so he can have his affair back. bob exists. he is but an easy representation or rather an easy escape from the horrors surrounding us. while the movie/show does rely on bob/the other world for dramatic effect and also to push the show towards a more horror inclined edge - the central philosophy remains as clear as day

we know most events that happen in the movie through accounts from the show yet due to this image we had been projecting onto laura, we always fail her to see a real person, we fail to see her suffering or to truly know her at all

and lastly, after seeing laura delving into sex work as a minor, abusing substances, being sexually abused by assholes including her own family, being left so absolutely alone; her death comes as a cathartic escape from it all. an angelic escape as she starts to cry tears from joy as the town that she had to exist in before this was torment every single second to exist in. we as viewers also find some comfort that despite this being another of the countless amount of atrocities committed against her. she will atleast find some relief in the other world

anurag delivers quite potentially the best work of his career and thats saying a lot

anurag seems to have been boxed in a box ever since the huge success of gangs and that’s understandable. gangs is one of the most finest movies to ever come out in parallel cinema of india. a parallel cinema film that burst through the thin wall separating it from mainstream cinema, exploding into a huge success [post theatrical]. this also inturn has people yearning to get that same thing from anurag. 

people want anurag to make another dev d or another gangs because well they are great films. and anurag has gathered this grim reality sort of image amongst the audience he has gathered. people dont want to see ‘almost pyaar’ centered around navigating teen relationships no fuck that give us nawaz running around with a gun

and when anurag does deliver a film as impressive and as poignant as mukkabaaz, people just give a light shrug because the grim tropes arent there; its a genre film which is accessible to audiences and thats derogatory to most pretentious cinephiles.

now finally to talk about the movie, while it is a genre film, its an excellently executed genre film. this film probably has some of the best acting performances of this century. has a soundtrack that could rival the likes of bhardwaj. shot in a way that is incredible to see. edited in such a crisp manner that time flies by. tackling socio-political issues in a way thats elegant and also poignant. yet, people dont want that, people dont want eclectic soundtracks from mr kashyap, they want blood. they dont want a romance depicted so pure and honest - no, make even the romance be problematic and then we will approve of the film. 

i realize i didnt talk much about the film but the film stands as a testament to how much hatred these snooty cinephiles harbour towards our cinema’s most unique quality of connecting with a larger audience. how much they would rather have a movie about a romance brewing in Benaras be made for their upper social class eye with ‘subtle symbolism’ so they could exotically experience it all and jerk off while the general, not as snooty, audience be left with nothing but mainstream regurgitated trash. this is how they find in themselves to rate a movie as excellent as this as 2 stars : “um actually lol anurag please give us more sneak peaks into your culture but please dont make all your characters human pls thats scary to imagine”

a trans woman as a protagonist to exploring the life of a sex worker to exploring the swirling vortex of the cybernet

dibakar has somehow pulled off the fucking impossible, as a 54 years old boomer, he has somehow made a fucking excellent sensible non-cringy anthology serving as a sequel to LSD following the same narrative structure and deriving from the same impressive cohesive found-footage type filming; dibakar uses whatsapp calls, zoom meetings, tv footage, youtube videos, live streams, cctv cameras to tell another set of titillating stories. as you should with a dibakar banerjee film, this film has tons of political commentary - some subtle, some not, and a lot of them drawn from real life incidents
alike the movie itself, i will divide my thoughts on the movie into their respective sections (even though there are some impressive overlaps in the otherwise standalone stories)

pt. 1 - love

the first part lands us into the world of noor, a trans woman, starring in a show called 'truth-ya-naach' (which is through several soundbites pronounced as 'chutiya naach' lol). dibakar definitely has a lot of first-hand experience to draw from in this section when it comes to the worldbuilding and it shows. noor is a trans woman who is unabashedly her and it is so fucking refreshing to see. this section of the movie definitely leans more on satire, almost a complete parody, than the others. the whole bits with anu malik, tushar kapoor and the whole show is funny. the constant absurd call-to-action overlays. the incredibly loud and jarring sound effects with back-to-back slowmos. "tum logo ke best truth moments off-cam hote hai yaar" lol

however, this doesn't mean it's devoid of any real political commentary or a divisive stand. a movie, produced by a mainstream bollywood producer, has a scene discussing vaginoplasty and its relative cost while also showing the sheer mockery we as a society still inflict upon trans folks.

the fact that there is a scene in a mainstream bollywood film where deadnaming a trans woman makes her go into a fiery fit as she should instead of some complacent cop out ass comical response makes me very happy. good start to the movie

pt. 2 - sex

we now delve into the life of a trans sex worker, kulu. kulu is a woman happily in a relationship with ajmal who loves her dearly.

we need to recall her and her life for a bit before i can delve into what I want to talk about - employed as a sanitation worker at a metro station's toilet (through some governmental initiative to hire more transgender employees). kulu is also a sex worker outside of her sanitation work and she is somehow able to juggle both of her jobs very well. that is until, one unfortunate day, a client of hers physically assaults her and leaves her body in a ditch badly bruised. through immense grit and just sheer helplessness in the face of survival in this expensive city, she shows up to work barely days after this horrific incident. like I mentioned earlier, this highlights something important.

trans people are some of the most marginalized in our indian society. ~96% of transgenders are declined jobs - forcing them to resort to other odd or low-paying jobs. forget employment, they are still ostracised and denied basic human status. people are still uncomfortable just sharing a public space with them. parents teach their kids to be wary of them. people "fear" them because of some bullshit mythological reason. they still try to make a living for themselves through some way or the other and yet unfortunately are at most able to secure a contractual blue-collar worker job and with that comes with the exploitation common amongst another marginalized group in our society. all of this happens while the actual decision makers tour the world, have extra-marital affairs while lacking an ounce of empathy - and anyone having even the smallest bit of conscience immediately renounces at the slightest bit of discomfort in the fear of the dent it could make on their privilege. while, in the end kulu and countless others like her end up in absolute despair losing the only few people they truly love

greatly fucking written

pt. 3 - dhokha

once I realized what they were doing, this is the part I was the least excited about. this is the part where I expected some obvious message along the lines of 'kids these days just vidya games' and well, while a valid point, not necessarily the most profound thing to use in a movie but oh boy was i so wrong

while this section does start off with the portrayal of a classic indian youtuber - loud inappropriate jokes, screaming at your teammates on any competitive game, obsessed with the numbers on their screen

this basic premise is however taken to a place so much grander

the life of this unsuspecting teen is in shambles with actions beyond his comprehension or control

ai is scary and so is our ever losing grip on reality as we escape further into our virtual reality headsets and wear AI powered chips and make AI "art" to avoid paying real artists but that is not a new statement or neither a statement that really could ever fit into a film. so how do you deliver a message that is at such odds with the medium? you use the medium's capabilities to its fullest

this really does feel like a new age we have ushered ourselves into as humanity. one rampant with misinformation. one rampant with tools so complex and powerful that it's impossible to discern real from fake, truth from lies, meaning from just about anything. this new phase is fucking shown to us and dibakar really fucking emphasises this while he uses the classic 2001 space odyssey audio as we much like the primates usher ourselves into an age barely familiar to us as the movie gradually builds and breaks into a cacophony of AI and ugly fucking virtual avatars as you the viewer are left to ponder over the world we are headed towards

hey ram is one of the most brilliant films that covers a major chunk of indian history in a way that is so sensible yet so engaging

it's a movie not interested in any one narrative except one of exploring empathy and the death of the aforementioned through indoctrination

the movie takes its time initially to build up its characters with amazingly charming performances from shahrukh khan, saurabh shukla, rani mukherjee and of course the brilliant kamal haasan

the pacing is ever so brilliant that it's astounding that a 3 hours movie breezes through while also covering a major event of our history in a 'semi-fiction' way

the dialogues also flow so fucking well and are conversational

the movie starts us off on the direct action day of august 16, 1946 and establishes everything but without the use of any big title cards establishing timelines and events but rather through the use of simple dialogues and events - i fucking love that

every prominent historical figure is also casted so fucking well, acted so fucking well that it's honestly absurd. suhrawardy is a 1-1 carbon copy, it is insane

it's also not just a simple historical drama interested in reenacting events but rather it's much more interested in dissecting human and the ease with which indoctrination could happen and leave a man becoming a broken husk

proper spoilers ahead, if you're reading this review still and haven't watched the movie yet. i would strongly recommend doing so. it's an excellent film that will not disappoint.

ram's wife is brutally raped and murdered in front of him by the people of the All India Muslim League as he is forced to helplessly watch - as were done to many families during the bengal riots on the direct action day

a propaganda film would've stopped there and been happy justifying an absolute murder revenge seeking to destroy everyone who would had the misfortune of being born into this religion

this movie however sends ram on a murderous rage definitely but until he discovers humanity. he discovers the people of the religion he so violently detests are similarly tragically depraved with their families having been given the same treatment. this isn't about a religion inciting violence but rather powerful figures trying to incite violence whether that be Jinnah or Savarkar.

ram eventually does believe that, yes while this religion does produce scum, it's gandhi. the one advocating for an end to this violence and very vehemently promoting hindu-muslim unity - that's the man to be blamed for all of this. he is the root cause of these riots since he wants to pretend that this religion isn't inherently full of blood hungry animals hoping to kill anyone in their way

this idea consumes ram completely until he is barely recognizable to anyone around him or even to the viewers - physically and metaphorically

ram's family hoping he moves on and marries again sees him be absolutely detached from anyone and anything. he is a man consumed by one thing and one thing alone. he goes and marries an extremely young bride

"bachi hai ye lekin"
"tujhe buddhi chaiye?"

this intellectual sensible guy who would not even drink alcohol is now complacent enough to agree to a marriage with a huge age difference because there is one that matters to him anymore - assassinating gandhi

his sensibilities which he has shoved deep down in a void do come out every once in a while and beckon him
in true shakespearean fashion, we see apparitions of people he has killed so far. blind child urging him, asking him "hey ram, mai kaise marri. bataun?"
all his wrong doings and trauma appear in front of him as vivid apparitions
until he shoves these sensibilities deep into the void where they are trying to come out from

he gets drawn more into the group of extremists trying to propagate this same belief
"hindu-muslims are brothers"
"oh like china-japan are brothers? like germany england?"

the extremists further help in muting and making sure his morality or guilt doesn't come out in even the slightest by making sure to say stuff like "killing in a war isn't murder" to justify killing innocent people

ram is a complete broken husk of a man absolutely consumed by what transpired contrasted to his ever so sweet wife
his ever so sweet wife with higher moralistic standards than him
his wife, devoting herself into understanding him and helping him despite his neglectful and problematic behaviour

there are so many things to love about this film but I have outlined most of the important aspects except the last one, the attention to visual storytelling

there is significant attention to using lynchian fever dreamish sequences and also using creative symbolisms like

maharashtra's old province king having hitler's picture hung on his wall as he gives a speech on the need to eliminate mahatma gandhi

and my favorite sequence, ever I think

gandhi’s image being shot alongside a pakistan flag which morphs into a swastika which then morphs into the swastika adopted by the nazis while the marathi visarjan dholaks turn into nazi march drums for a second and then morphs into a lotus eventually breaking into a 2001 esque cacophony eventually ending in a marathi dance number holy fuck

a transition from an eye to a fever dream ass sequence where ram practices his shooting

to wrap it all off, all the events in the story are done on a deathbed as an unknown old man's family stands around him, listening to him until we finally realize that's ram surrounded by a muslim family he calls his own.
because, eventually through his friends. through the ordinary people outside his extremist circle, he regains empathy slowly until he is not the unrecognizable monster consumed by hatred

"maine us darinde ko kabhi nahi dekha. ye mera bhai ram hai"

dharavi is a fever dream of a movie that is also somehow able to so fucking grounded in the reality in the great slums of dharavi

for a area so prominent in mumbai's culture - hosting over a million people in just 600 acres of land - we have seen severe neglect in telling their stories except poverty porn or ultra unrealistic fantastical pieces

sudhir mishra has absolutely achieved the perfect storytelling for dharavi relying on arc of characters that are indirectly able to critique the overall workings of mumbai suburban

i cant sing enough praises of om puri, shabana azmi, raghubir yadav and almost everyone. they all do a great job

renu saluja has to be one of the best film editors we have ever had, may she rest in peace

there is a palpable sense of claustrophobia that permeates through the film depicting daily lives of the people in dharavi, even as I write this review and yet it's not shown to be all gleam

despite the despondent neglect shown by the people in power towards them, there is this sense of resistance and enthusiasm to do something greater. almost irreverence to not be complacent with the cards they have been dealt which is something i have rarely seen when filmmakers explore these regions

like mentioned before, those are also on spectrums. we have moments of gloom and these brief moments of joy all bundled together to depict what dharavi actually is

anil kapoor and madhuri dixit doing some kick-ass shit and it all being consumed by the people to get a brief relief from the daily life they have to endure highlights an important thing about our indian cinema and how it fundamentally differs from cinema around the world

we need the over the top cheesy action sequences with larger-than-life heroes because for a lot of our population, thats their escapism - a brief respite from the conditions they live in everyday

while us fancy privileged people could comfortably enjoy our latest indie flick with our mubi subscription and have some 'introspection' with the movie, these people need something that makes them forget their life for a few hours and gawk at this alternate dreamland

lastly, the fellini-esque dream sequences depicting om puri's character flirting with madhuri dixit is what the movie is all about. madhuri dixit is the unattainable far away dream for him. she is the beauty icon, she is the luxury icon. she represents a lifestyle he hopes to achieve. she represents a place that he hopes to eventually get to. all that stands between him and madhuri is money and the cards he has been dealt with in the roulette of capitalism. a roulette of unprivileged birth happenstance.

"is there a god?"

women characters who are not just for prosthetics but actually stand up for themselves and have their own volitions - cementing friendships that are not heteronormative either where a man and a woman can be friends without necessary sexual undertones

“the demon living in roshomon fled in the fear of the ferocity of a man”

fargo is in constant dissonance with the film’s presentation and the events that transpire - it makes it all so interesting

i haven't recently found a film that tickled my brain in a way where it was a gradual realisation of what the film is aiming to do

fargo is about horrific events in the state of Minnesota that eventually leads to a cop trying to piece it all together. sounds horrible enough and yet the way its presented and the way characters behave and talk almost makes it feel like its a sitcom

the filmmakers create this beautiful dissonance deeper as the movie goes on as it borders on feeling like a comedy yet the cinematic shots, brooding soundtrack tell a different story

“based on a true incident” it starts with and gets you absolutely hooked. the poster of the movie also signals a dark engaging thriller while its an engaging and great story - it’s not shown in the way as is done with the movies in this genre, they play into the genre’s strength to deliver an astounding end result

and i think what it achieves is brilliant

the film’s overly caricatured characters work so much in highlighting whats so important about this whole incident

this move allows the horrible kidnappers/criminals to be deglamorized heavily - in contrast to other “deeper” psychological thrillers that portray these villains and people start using them as their wallpapers (without also being so unrealistic that it becomes satire)

the film’s exploration of this very tendency is like few other movies. show dont tell is taken to a level of absolute delight. i loved every second of it

a towering achievement on using animation as a medium to its fullest. miyazaki utilises his talented animators to make an experience that sucks us all in at once. the whole movie reeks of characters so endearing and charming yet having a central dilemma they are a part of. the protagonist of our story isnt really the protagonist but rather just a vessel so that actualisations and realisations could be had by every other character and its amazing. 

philosophically and thematically, its so incredibly dense. the overreaching habit of man vs the oh so divine and supernatural ways of nature are embodied and visualised in a way that its an incredibly endearing experience and yet somehow the overreaching human isnt also extremely vilified but shown with a convincing enough backstory to it all.

its a great experience and it cements my theory that if your name has miyazaki in it, you automatically make great pieces of art

being a third world country with a culture miles different than the landscape of almost any other country, i always write off foreign countries suddenly being interested in our country’s problems and politics because more often than not its just this exotic misery porn for them - where in their perspective is to look at the human beings living in india as these extreme caricatures of “colors”, diversity and other similar bullshit

despite that, i think the documentary succeeds because no matter their intentions, compiling and assembling horrifying things that happen in our country is as riveting and horrifying as anything else

this is not fiction, this is not cherrypicked either - these are actual things transpiring day by day that are validated by the most educated people, colleagues, people living in tier 1 cities, people who have access to the internet and movies and its so miserably sad

this documentary was banned and journalists will get arrested. opposition will be thrown out of the parliament. rapists will be welcomed with open arms by the leaders. excellent talent (athletes/engineers/doctors) will quit and be just another person to go as the media will focus on the grand inauguration of the ram mandir. but i believe in my country and just like how indira gandhi’s unchecked power abuse birthed bjp and eventually mutated into this monstrosity. bjp’s power abuse will sooner or later give us an india which is just and welcoming

its very rare that a movie leaves me absolutely dumbstruck and this is one of those movies

the movie which is based on the play bhavni bhavai is entirely in gujurati and yet every word uttered comes through the language barrier and hits you like a pair of bricks

one of the most commendable parts about this entire movie has to be the sociopolitical commentary being done through satire. theres an undertone of black comedy through its entire runtime and drawing caricatures of brahmin's atrocities is a very unique, refreshing yet gripping way to go about a movie

few of my favorite 'comedic' moments have to be:

every second that shah is on the screen

the james bond spy character

"my donkey is more handsome than most men here"

when the brahmin has to take a bath after he gets in the contact of a dalit's shadow but being hit by a dirty dog and falling into mud isn’t enough of a reason for him to take a bath [showcasing the brahmin's inherent concept of being pure and clean just being a farce to feel superior as he neglects actual hygiene and morals]

since we have started talking about it, showcase of brahmins and their atrocities are on full and clear display here even though I truly feel a movie is unable to capture the extent of their actions

from the brahmin pandit waffling about a bunch of traditions and sacredness - while he eyes up a random woman taking a bath near the river and also accepts bribes from other kingsmen

"we must maintain the social system, if we remove the identifiers we force on them, they will want everything next"

the utter uselessness of the "upper caste" as the whole kingdom falls to ruin because a few "lower caste" people stop showing up to run their whole operations [and i think a true parallel can be drawn to our current times with the amount of essential blue collar workers still being dalits]

the movie is also a musical with several songs being kafkaesque renditions with heart-wrenching lyrics while others being joyous celebratory tracks

"the sun and moon mean nothing to me - dig is all I do in life - still the earth yields no water - all i do is labour and toil - i too desire, i too thirst"

even rewriting it reminds me of it all

if you have are still reading but haven't watched the movie I would urge you to and highly recommend doing so - its a worthwhile experience

"they rape our women, they burn our houses. don't you feel anything?" is said as jivo looks directly at the camera as the film directly talks to us and that's what seperates this film from most others

despite the fantastical, history-altering style [the one tarantino very famously uses], the film scopes us the viewers and reminds us that these victories and quips are all fictional while the sufferings are very much real and still persist

"who are you talking to?"
"the ones who are cocooned in their darkness"
"if only they could see"

even after the joyous ending, the abrupt cut reminds us that this sedating tale was everything but real and the real life still remains tough and unforgiving for them but mehta doesn't stop there. another layer is peeled back even further, where instead of any actors, we see clips of our very real independence movement being transposed onto the screen in a harsh, abrasive sequence urging us the viewers, the letterboxd users, the "cinephiles" to look beyond the movie as a means of entertainment, "good writing" and realize the gravity of some of these social structures that persist way beyond every 2001 space odyssey reference

fucking cinema

reviews.film: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
reviews.review:
theres a scene where as the kids lay on the bed, a book called “impressionists” lay on the table

now, im not sure that this was not intended but i think that book describes the movie very aptly

according to wikipedia, impressionism was a 19th century art movement, characterised by relatively small, thin, yet visible brush strokes, open composition, emphasis on accurate depiction of light in its changing qualities (often accentuating the effects of the passage of time), ordinary subject matter, unusual visual angles, and inclusion of movement as a crucial element of human perception and experience 

killing of a sacred deer is an impressionist piece of art that takes the doctor-patient relationship and flips it to the doctor begging the person to help them out, save their family’s lives. heavy munna bhai mbbs influence I would say. 

what i love the absolutely most out of everything else is the way its put together

it is so impressive the surreal undertone the film is able to achieve despite there being zero surreal visual element. the film’s surrealism further helps in hooking you to the movie since the peculiar circumstances surrounding the movie seem to us like a classic surrealist metaphor. the film uses and relies on the viewer’s past lynch or fellini watching experience to further immerse us into this bizarre world

this surrealist quality is achieved through multiple things like this eclectic background score that rivals eraserhead or the shining in the way it feels like its stabbing you multiple times. through the awkward acting performances by such great actors. through the editing being so methodical and yet feels abrasive. through the camera angles being so stabilised at moments but still feeling so unsettling

another thing that is impressive (which i realised after watching and googling) is how Iphigenia’s story is modernly readapted into a contemporary tale

there are so many impressive things about this movie but lastly, remember the impressionism I talked about initially? the fact that some scenes are directly inspired by edward hopper’s paintings adds an extra layer of validity to it

a great film with so much to love it for

“izzat ameero ka shauk hai”

a triumph of a movie that despite being a period drama excels not through some elaborate vfx or physical sets but rather the way every character is written and performed

colonial india had human abuse like no time else and to an extent not imaginable - seeing it being realised not just in a plain oh its so sad way but rather through the perspective of a woman in one of those villages is very powerful 

through all the horribleness of the colonial villages, a beautiful humanitarian undertone permeates the move

“agar marad bahaar samay na guzarein to kya kahenge? itna bada mukhiya aur ek aurat nahi rakh sakta?”
“mai aurat nahi hu?”
“tum biwi ho”

men, powerful or not, remain complacent - perpetuating the horribleness of the colonisers. they berate other men, disregard women and their rights while living a life devoid of any productivity or meaning

“aurat ki akal ko hi khyaal aa sakta hai roti ka”

the women end up doing all the work, end up providing for the family and having any resemblance of empathy towards their own kin

the coloniser beats someone for a broken record when he has a borderline infinite supply of them is contrasted with beautiful pure precious reactions of the villagers to the music playing

“namak haram?”
“tera namak to aaj se waise hi zeher hai”

despite having all the privileges, powers and material things, his insecure personality and ego is full blown when one of the women don’t immediately fold in awe looking at his things. 

“beti ko school le jaa rahi hu”
“isse shaadi kaun karega phir? ladka nahi hua tab bhi kuch nahi kaha”

an amazing film with some great performances and writing that will leave you terrified at times and grinning at others. om puri standing his guard through everything is one of the most bad ass things ever on film

cinema

sardar udham singh is a movie made in a way that breaks most bollywood conventions and its a delight to watch

from the cinematography to the narrative structure is all in service of a story that is very important to be told

the movie subverts most people’s expectations by not making the assassination the climactic ending but rather showing us the “how” the climax and its harrowing

the ideologies are also so well researched and its refreshing to see the ideologies of great revolutionaries like bhagat singh told in a way that reflects their actual ideology - from his atheism to his openly socialist beliefs

a movie that is entirely about one man’s heroic patriotic action also somehow avoids all jingoism that would’ve plagued any movie made in our subcontinent about the same subject 

and lastly, the characterisation of all the historical figures is nothing short of astounding. despite having sparse historical accounts via written records and the very few anecdotal accounts, the characters come alive and seeing them is hard hitting and will leave you in tears

thank you sircar sahaab 🙏

Angoor is a super well-crafted movie that oozes meticulous love for the play through its every pore and it sprinkles everywhere over the frame

the movie starts, not with a lousy text describing how it was inspired by Shakespeare’s “Comedy of Errors” but rather an entire voiceover intro, which first describes who Shakespeare was before delving into the significance of the play and how it has been adapted - which greatly signifies Gulzar’s intent to not put a legal disclaimer but rather share his love towards Shakespeare by spreading it as wide as possible

from the intro sequence itself, its hilarious and doesn’t stop being hilarious until it ends. the intro hand crafted graphic sequence is so well made and perfectly sets the tone for the movie

every actor kills it with their performance. there is an air of novelty in seeing 70’s mumbai realised in this way too. the songs are not the highlight but dont falter obviously because of Gulzar ji’s penmanship 

the editing and camera work are the home run highlights. from detective noises to the music phasing in/out in a simulated doppler effect, its all so fun

i love gulzar ji, kumar, dipti and this movie

a quintessential film to show the power of simplicity and being certain about what you aim to achieve with your movie

the whole milieu of the movie is so well setup that its hard to not get fully immersed on every second of everything happening in the screen. it doesn’t have to be something of a grand scale thats happening and yet you cant take your eyes off for a second

the writing compliments everything about the milieu in this grand symphony that leaves you utterly mesmerised 

the actors play their roles to perfection - down to the child actors. an air of effortlessness permeates through the entire acting but retains a dramatic undertone

all the different characters breathe and are animated in a way that its hard to ever lose empathy for anyone - its very well written 

its wholesome, gutwrenching and yet their unfortunate circumstances underly all the writing leaving you truly not upset at anyone except the way sometimes our world functions

cinema

this is the exact type of film that makes me not like films. this is the film that makes me so incredibly hopeless about the type of cinema that is appreciated 

this film has a great interesting premise that it just butchers and takes nowhere 

the film reeks of the pretentious exoticness with which a lot of filmmakers view poor people

every scene is acted to perfection with the brilliant actors yet everything from the dialogues to the sequencing leaves you utterly disgusted 

the film treats its characters as being merely symbolic while also wanting to bask in its realism - you cant have your cake and eat it too

every character behaves with such confusing eccentricity that its impossible it’s intentional 

a pragmatic woman who works through late stages of her pregnancy is upset at a gun at home just so the plot point could pivot towards making the gun be symbolic and metaphorical

our protagonist is a timid empathetic person who is unable to scare away monkeys with his voice but still chooses to be eccentric at every possible moment (which is again just so the metaphors and symbolism could be shoved down our throats)

the ending tops it all up with an incoherent mess littered with provoking images just so a circlejerk validation could be had from other pretentious filmmakers 

a film that does so much to disrespect what films should actually be about. a film that isnt made from a deeper place of empathy but rather scientifically orchestrated ticking boxes for everything that is appreciated by the high brow crowd

fuck rajkumar hirani and his stupid ass emotional ass movies, stupid films that make me bawl

okay, now that that is out of the way, i will always have rajkumar hirani as my favourite contemporary indian cinema director just because every movie the man has released or will ever release has firstly a lot of love put towards it and secondly it ends up influencing masses like few films usually do

we talk about how films are effective in protesting, educating, entertaining yet for most movies the message remains either too obtuse for the majority of the audience to understand or too one dimensional that the audience just doesn’t want to go through a 3 hours slog to be preached at or lastly they become a comedy making light of the matter to the point of it undermining their supposed “cause” and harming it

hirani, throughout his career, has done such a fine walk across dense topics while he makes sure his films are entertaining. and this in turn has real world effect. to this day, i remember the multiple conversations happening in my village regarding the medical industrial complex and on having empathy towards blue collar workers after munna bhai mbbs came out, i remember the conversation on god and worship after pk came out, i remember the conversation on engineering, mental health and suicidal tendencies in my village after 3 idiots. all this happened because of a few films. not insinuating that hirani is solely responsible but plays a major part in doing this sweet, positive entertaining and informative. 

just like hirani’s previous works. this one, also does everything in classic hiraniesque fashion. we have the fundamental societal issue, we have the entertaining stories, we have great performances/musicals and we have shahrukh. i will snide at all the professional letterboxd critics or critics in general because some movies have so much going for them with so much love that its okay to not be the most hyper critical nitpicking smart ass all the time

watch the movie, you owe it to yourself and you owe it to good filmmakers to support them

spoilers below, you should avoid seeing if you havent seen

the way hirani handles the story is empathetic and the way it gets delivered is also very visual and direct

the runtime of 3 hours breezes through

vicky kaushal’s performance is incredible and the immolation scene is still fresh on me

the comedy bits are also refreshing and funny - im very happy it doesnt rely on “english is tough” trope for too long

taapse is great and so is shahrukh. and seeing vishnu kaushal was such a delight!

i dont have much except disjointed thoughts and some tears about the movie but hope this long rant was worth reading

pyaasa is a movie that shouldn’t be tainted by the grotesque romanticisation of it by people on social media claiming stuff like “underrated masterpiece it flopped but look how classic”; i heavily reject your misery porn

pyaasa was a commercial hit with its songs reaching the masses with astute success. i have memories of singing a few songs with my father and my father singing few with my grandfather - thats how influential it was 

the movie throughout its runtime presents us with vijay and his lens with which he views the world.  vijay is an impractical man and yet for him it comes from a deeper place of yearning for something that he is unable to find in this material world

pyaasa is very much a heavily self-referential work to the point its almost autobiographical. following dutt’s infidelity, we see waheeda falling in love in reel with him 

dutt also reinforces his suffering with jesus and its oh so beautiful in the numerous shots of him with white light behind and his arms to the side 

the songs are poetic and so is the visual language. great film.

donkey in a brahmin village gets as absurd and satirical as it sounds like but it does so with an air of genuineness

inspired by au hasard balthazar which is in turn said to be inspired by dostoyevsky

borrowing from nietzsche’s “can an ass be tragic? to be crushed by a burden that one can neither bear nor throw off? the case of the philosopher” - the movie gets a donkey inside a brahmin village 

the layers of social critiques are plenty and admittedly some didnt become apparent to me 

“are you aware of the donkey’s atrocities?” they discuss as a brahmin man rapes a mute servant just seconds ago

a philosopher caring for a donkey becomes the heated topic of discussion as the other common atrocities are not even paid attention to

i am not entirely sure of the intended message but for me the image of a donkey being blamed for all the nuisances just because the donkey doesn’t speak is very poetic to me

the donkey gets placed in situations where it doesn’t belong and that is used as an excuse by the brahmins to inflict violence - as do and have the brahmins done throughout history

the image of an innocent donkey, being dragged around, being blamed, being denied a right to exist just because some other brahmins wanted to do things that could be in the slightest important 

the power of ignorance and mob decision making that leads to the suffering of an innocent donkey

of a brahmin man, philosopher and good willed himself, unintentionally perishing a donkey and denouncing himself in the eyes of other brahmins just because he wanted to save that donkey from the evil acts being inflicted on it

all these images are presented with a cinematography style very stark and raw - and a background score as eclectic as the movie

john abraham’s important film that converts almost a fever dream of a film into a cohesive watch

my favourite sequence of the film would be:
“worship even dirt, excrement - even donkey, mud for god is in every atom” is chanted as a bunch of brahmins beat an innocent donkey to death

ballad of a white cow is a movie that will have you enchanted as soon as it begins and will not leave you until the credits roll in

there is so much to love about this that i'm not sure where to begin

the performances from everyone are great, the way its shot, the pacing. all of the usual tick boxes

guilt and grief are two powerful emotions. dealing with both require a lot of strength. people help. the same people who get inflicted with these emotions from a fault maybe not so much their own but just how the larger world works around us. but, a guilty person is guilty despite him being an empathetic human being repenting everything they did. a grieving person truly grieves for as long as they live even if they might try to move on for short pockets of time to get themselves on with their lives. in the end, humans are just a bunch of beings hoping they don't become a cautionary tale or a tragic ballad

this is what my 4th grade teacher shabnam wanted to happen to our class

the movie is honestly a fun movie which doesn’t waste too much time in trying to be more profound than the premise is

the action and the violence is not the most stylistic but remains semi-realistic atleast

the best part about the movie is the humor, lol. i just want to point out some of my favourites below:

the lady being overly excited about murder instructions

the cookies that he devours 

the nerd reciting math formulas as he panics🤣

there are also some devastating moments like the one where someone is getting murdered with several bullets after saying they have a crush on someone - and the murderer puts a megaphone to their mouth to amplify their whimpering goddamn

emotional storybeats didn't connect with me but that’s alright

and lastly, the girl chasing after the disgusting sexual assaulter and stabbing him in the penis is top 10 cinematic moments of all time

reviews.film: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
reviews.review:
there is one thing that Greta Gerwig said that i really keep coming back to

when Greta was asked what according to her is the definition of cinema, her answer was as follow:

"you just know it when you see it. it just doesn't miss you. from the first frame itself, you know when there's an author behind it" and i have truly found it true for every movie i have ever enjoyed. i obviously still give chances to movies that dont click instantly too but in general its a true scale

this movie severely feels the antithesis of what Greta was defining

the movie seems to be more interested in creating something with the intention of it earning praises rather than something that came from their heart

posturing and ticking all the right boxes that will appeal to our modern crowd as opposes to telling a story that the maker's really connect with

every dialogue feel so utterly hollow. every line uttered with inflections and framing such that people could record it and post it somewhere

every frame made by the filmmaker not in a way that facilitates storytelling but rather so people could take stills from the movie

there are a few nice things about it but despite that it ends up feeling like such a carefully orchestrated attempt at being profound and intellectual not because the story warrants that but because they wanted to signal that they are profound

"maaya duniya se bohot alag hai. lekin kya karein, mai kaafi sadhaaran hu"

ijaazat is a movie with its fists forming a firm grip on intricacies of relationships. written and directed by gulzar sahib, you should expect all the usual poetic routines where dialogues will pierce through your heart, songs will make you weep but one of the most striking things about this movie is

the respect that gulzar ji has for the audience - there is absolutely no spoonfeeding or big ear piercing background musical score inferences towards something being good or bad. its just a refreshing portrayal of their relationships akin to the french new wave

down to the very structure of the film, the film has a non linear structure with jumps in time happening without any cue cards or titles; if you don't pay attention you will probably miss a lot of context but yet it's never jarring or too much to process

everyone in the cast has an amazing performance and the shammi kapoor cameo is nice to see

now before i end this, a little about the dynamics:
mohinder was a guy who despite having a wonderful wife couldn't let go of his past - couldn't gather the guts to say a proper goodbye to a significant person of his past. instead, he chose an annoying complacency, dragging his wife and his ex-lover along while giving none of the proper closure - while absolving himself of all his sins under the guise of "oh look im so honest"

sudha with stark contrast after making the decision to leave, actually left. actually moved on in her life. giving proper closure to herself and also making sure she doesn't drag anyone along in this mist of hazy bollywoodesque love dreaminess. she let go of Mohinder's maachis without letting go of the memories and respect she had for him

what a movie

it just doesn't miss you

from the first shot, first frame of the film, it doesn't miss you

varda's way of telling a story is like no other and is so fundamental to the french new wave

dealing with death in art is often very farce and often focused on intellectualizing the concept of death or making it aesthetic

"death is real, someone's there and then they are not. and its not for singing about, its not for making into art" - phil elverum

and yet, varda doesn't make light of the concept and neither does she try to make it into some high brow snob portrayal of the same

dont get me wrong, the movie is very beautifully shot and some lines had me staring at the screen in absolute awe but fundamentally-

the movie deals with the anxiety that comes with knowing you're about to die - knowing your time in life is limited. these imposing test results follow our protagonist throughout the runtime and yet when her self-actualisation and character development has happened (akin to taking off the sunglasses as in that short film) - its not only the character that has this self actualisation but also us. and when the results are actually out, us alike the protagonist have a calm acceptance of it after we have all taken off our melancholic glasses

brilliant film

after having seen the disastrous goldfish, i was very much praying to god that this better not be in the same league and thankfully it wasn't!

avinash, after his amazing patal lok direction switches to a very endearing story and its not jarring at all - he is quite versatile and it shows

the movie has some very pretty sets and set pieces which will stay with you (the ferris wheel, man). the konkan setting also lends so much to the movie feeling so intimate and grounded

the actors are all great actors who have proven themselves already and they once more do a great job. for me, this might be shephali's best performance and that's saying a lot because she is incredibly skilled and talented at what she does

the whole movie retains a fine balance between the dialogues being profound and also being the way that people usually talk. that fine line is hard to achieve usually and that was done very on point alongside some humor sprinkled in. and it all made sense when i saw that the dialogues were infact written by varun grover!

for me, the movie creates some great characters who are all very endearing at times but also end up existing as seperate pockets as opposed to meshing together in an interesting way - i am not sure if that makes sense lol but i am unable to articulate it better than that right now

overall, the movie is pretty with some great performances and an overall touching plot with some minor missing pieces that might click for me on a rewatch

when scorsese talks about cinema, its easy to snide and pass him off as just a snob who doesn't like fun movies - but this movie embodies what scorsese keeps talking about and the fact that this is truly cinema. this movie embodies the power that cinema as an art form truly holds. walking out of the theatres, you will have learned about something from perspectives of people you would've never gotten to see unless you had actively seeked them out. empathy and growth by just paying a small amount of money while also being entertained on your off day. this is cinema

talking about the movie, it's very tough to wrap your head around the fact that this man is 80 years old and still firing at all fronts delivering a movie that can rival every contemporary director and as well as his own legendary works

the movie is over 3 hours 20 minutes long and yet the actual runtime won't be felt by you at all (by your physical body maybe since you will be sitting for a long time). every shot and every frame is carefully orchestrated with style so good that you can screenshot every frame

the movie's cast are all obviously very acclaimed and incredible actors and yet they somehow deliver a performance that will stand toe to toe with their past hits. yet despite all the big names, lily gladstone takes the crown. she delivers a performance that will leave you mesmerized every second. a performance that will make you weep and feel the intensity of some of the things happening in the movie

the entirety of the movie is also propelled to new heights by the incredible music. this isn't your regular modern hans zimmeresque orchestration but instead a score that stirs you in a way that remains intune with the movie's setting

its very evident how much scorsese cares about the actual topic being dealt with and his effort is very much visible in every second of the film

the idea of white people "civilizing" different indian tribes is an idea inherently rooted in a lot of hatred that a lot of white men through history have had towards everyone even slightly dissimilar. this same thing is also happening in realtime in modern india where a lot of the tribes in north-eastern part of india are still being put under rigorous scrutiny and an attempt is being made to "civilize" them. its disheartening that what happened to the native Americans of america continues to happen to multiple tribes such as the nagas in India to this day while most people in the country consider north east to not be a real part of india

anyway, i digress, the movie is a poignant work showcasing things that are of great value to this day. showcasing how civil the tribes actually were and contrasting it with the "civilized" nature of the white people - being rowdy, being loud and being treating everything as a tradeable asset under capitalism. mollie's character is one with great integrity, patience and passion; juxtaposed with the rowdy, spineless and impatient character of ernest

so many emotions but to sum it up

unequivocally a statement on what cinema is supposed to be

a somber, geniune movie telling a saccharine yet at times a tragic story about one upsc aspirant that is easily extrapolated and applicable to tons of people attempting to crack the civil services exam every year

every character is so charming and endearing - every actor gives an incredible performance

vvc flexes his directorial muscles by giving some great sequences. vvc ushers mainstream bollywood into a respectful place where the maker's respect the audience [as he had done with his earlier works]. there is no generic sad music playing at the sad story beats to make you feel like aww thats sad but rather the rawness of the performances and the writing to do the same. there are no stereotypical tropes either but rather a refreshing geniune way of exploring rural india and their experiences in urban india.

vvc draws from his previous works and their incredibly clean editing and sound design. a lot of the moments are accentuated by very deliberate sound design while also acting as a storytelling device rather than relying on exposition

to package it all up, its based on a true story!

great film. vikrant massey is excellent, vvc is so back, movies are so back

my friend rohan had been pestering me for ages to watch this movie and for one reason or another, we just never ended up watching until yesterday

going in, i was expecting a mindless action flick - and since he is a huge fan of Hrithik, i assumed that was the reason we were watching but i was pretty pleasantly surprised

dont get me wrong, there is still a lot of action and a lot of it also falls into the usual boring action trope but a lot of the action is stylish too which makes it fun to watch

the story is accentuated by the classic tale of vikram betal which makes a lot of the action and character development so much more fun since you get to draw parallels

the makers also put in other symbolic devices such as a physical line, the way their clothes switch colors and eventually converge; its all very fun

seeing Lucknow and Kanpur with all its kulcha nihari and biryani awesomeness is also pretty fun lol

the one thing that stops this from being an even better movie is the sloppy editing and background score

the editing is so lazy, so hasty, so badly done that its hard to imagine how someone dropped the ball this hard. the background score is also the most numbing generic thing to have been conjured by the makers. alcoholia is a track that even my friend, who owns everything related to hritikh and has him as his pfp, even he couldnt defend it

regardless, a very fun movie with some good acting performance from everyone involved, fun story telling narratives held back by piss poor editing and music

i wouldve never thought in a million years i would ever smile a lot, almost cry on a movie about redditors but here we go

being someone who had followed the whole wsb fiasco very closely, just seeing the whole thing being realized on a big screen with major actors playing the roles was a surreal experience

the whole movie works in ways i didnt imagine it would - when i first heard about it, my assumption was seeing a ton of overly dramatic fictionalized accounts of everything that went down during the wsb gamestop run but i was pleasantly surprised by the accuracy

whether its accuracy in recreating dfv's videos/posts to the random twitter spaces or the actual discussion points of wsb degenerates or using the relevant 2020-2021 bangers, it was all really nice

one thing that makes it really shine is the characterizations of everyone. from melvin capital to robinhood - they spent a ton of time researching and also filling in the blanks creatively as to what their reactions would've been to everything going down and how they wouldve reacted. this in turn gave some solid characters which i think would resemble very closely to their real life counterparts. the scene where melvin capital's congressional hearing has a few minutes of making sure they sit in a damp room where their sea side view or their wine collection or the fact that they were born into privilege is all omitted

one subplot i was rejecting initially was stonksmom but i got warmed up to it as the movie progressed

paul dano and almost everyone really knock it out of the park. pete davidson is annoying

knowing the real life end to this whole saga, seeing the end credits and the SEC's reaction to this whole thing made me quite sad lol

the only negative is i think the editing/cinematography. which would've benefited from a more adam mcckayesque fictionalized documentary style

overall, a very solid movie. and one that i didnt expect to be this good

parineeta is the retelling of another saratchandra banerjee's classic that remains in the same league potent as devdas' retelling over decades in indian cinema

saif ali khan, sanjay dutt, vidya balan, and the rest of the cast are all very swiftly playing off of each other and establishing real on screen chemistry - not a single miss

the soundtrack is, as we all know, one of the best conjured by hindi cinema; it not being on Spotify is a serious crime lol

its also shot so gloriously and the sets, costumes all play well into it

now that's all out of the way, lets talk about two things i have been yearning to talk about

firstly, the editing
for all the things this movie does great, the editing is absolutely perfect. from the rhythmic jump cuts during the musical numbers to the way parallels are blended between both the main characters with musical notes acting as the transition markers. from the first scene of the movie to the end, a meticulous care is given to every aspect of the editing process and its very much appreciated

and lastly, the story [spoilers ahead]

through the movie's runtime i was very much immersed, engaged and pretty much understood the decisions considering the character's psyche. understood how shekhar's jealousy and the abrasive, manchildesque love manifested into all those horrible acts which make him pretty despicable. understood how girish's character was a nice person who fell for lolita but failed to calculate if she had desires for the same. after all this i had the firn belief that shekhar was a horrible person due to the ways he acted towards lolita. girish was pretty mild and normal. and hence it was weird to grasp why lolita would go for shekhar. i left the movie with a bad taste - the entire runtime had been great but the ending made me sad

after a few hours that the movie was over, it hit me. the movie is about lolita. lolita is an endearing, charismatic, kind and loving person who understands everyone's problems. despite of whatever she goes through, she stands on her own. and she loves shekhar; has loved him since they were little kids. she has always been endeared by his kindness as a kid. she has seen him transform into this not so pleasant manchild year after year due to his family's general outlook. she has seen the toxicity that runs in his father and how some of it has been endowed onto him. she loves him and understands the reasons behind it, too. she sees the person who loves her very dearly yet fails to ever translate into his actions. does this justify any of the horribleness shekhar does? if it was upto to me, i would make sure lolita never gets back with shekhar. but its not about you or me. its about lolita - parineeta - the married woman

phew, its hard to talk about the merits of a documentary about something so horrific

the 2006 noida serial murder case was a case which was very horrific and spine chilling with its trials still ongoing

i want to steer away from the subject matter but rather talk about the actual making of this documentary

i think the documentary is very well done and stands as an archival piece rather than something done to intice and excite people

a lot of complaints about it being too slow or dragged out are quite wrongly placed since how else would we ever get to hear the feelings of everyone involved (the accused and the victims alike)

the film also doesn't steer too much into being a tragic art dorian gray esque portrayal of the ordeal either but rather uses cinematography to further solidify the places its shot at instead of romanticize it or make it into "tragic cinema"

a must watch regardless because of the great work that has went into the research and the non-titillating unbiased take it presents on it

hindi cinema is really killing it this year with such progressive yet gripping movies!

thank you for coming is a great film with its heart at the right place

following omg 2 on its heels of making sex a not-so-tabboo topic and talking about it openly, thank you for coming carries the torch forward towards the actual act of sex

a lot of movies with progressive ideas and good intentions usually unfortunately fall into the trope of:

a) being overly sexual and tacky to the point of alienating audience and smothering all story beats
b) being too preachy and hence neglecting having an actual story behind the whole movie experience - wherein the movie starts playing like a sermon as opposed to a film

thank you for coming does neither!

it remains a very entertaining comedy with the actual severe epidemic of men ignoring women's sexual needs acting as the backdrop at times and when it is in the forefront, it handles it with care

the whole cast is very charismatic and bhumi is such a brilliant actress - its always so fun to see her on the screen [some men in the movie have questionable acting skills lol]

the drama and the low of the movie gets so low and depressing but thankfully follows with a much earned climax too

the musical numbers are honestly the worst part of the entire thing - they just dont fit or arent bangers either

there are a lot of references too! from veer zaara to sholay to an entire reenactment of the iconic ekta kapoor tv serial intro, very fun!

the worst part of the movie has to be making us believe that karan kundra is somehow too hot for bhumi pednekar

based on the infamous emergency of india - this film was banned during its initial release date and with some negatives being burned by supporters but regardless we have the film archived thankfully

the movie begins with a brilliant song sequence, song and a cry out to Mahatma Gandhi (sung by kishore kumar)

the sequence keeps highlighting the atrocities with heavy symbolism superimposed on top of it [you can draw so much parallel to present times lol]

and then the movie begins. the movie is a meta-ish comedy with a heavy emphasis and focus on mocking everything including the forced vasectomy procedures to the bollywood industry

for the former, the movie's entire timeline being this only. some standout scenes being two volunteers taking two volunteers in for vasectomy thinking they are tricking each other since they got paid based on how many people were neutered

the latter being, the meta comedy starting itself from the main cast. the main cast features duplicates of all major bollywood stars, namely, anitav bacchan, shahi kapoor, sev anand, rakesh khanna, kanoch kumar, kannauj kumar. johar casts himself in the movie as johar. all the songs are also parodies of famous hindi songs - damadam mast kalandar, aaj hai koi bahaar, kal hoga wo andar - its all pretty fun

despite its many many faults, its worth celebrating it because its historically important and an important event of a regime trying to ban people's expressions. India's archival systems not being the best so far (improving a lot). this is paramount. there was not a letterboxd page for it either and i had to go in and curate that. a not so great film but an important film none the less

reviews.film: Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance)
reviews.review:
did not expect this while going in for this movie but i am pretty pleasantly surprised

birdman is a movie which has multiple layers to it, out of which, i should admit i havent grapsed fully the intentions of each (rewatches might help) but regardless these are my interpretations

riggan is a faded actor whos glory days are behind him. having been part of a big comic book franchise movies once upon a time and this is what forms the crux

riggan's past in the form of the superhero he used to play talks to him wherever he goes

as riggan lies sad, despondent, depressed - this voice reminds him of the greater times when he was loved and cherished by all the fans ["pimple riddled video game nerds" according to the movie lol]

the camera and the movie follows riggan and his psyche; as such surreal imageries all throughout are riggan's psyche manifesting in different ways

his past self "haunts" him in unconvential ways where as instead of reminding him of the horrible past - it beckons him to seek that same level of stardom and "satisfaction" he had with his life back then
this is directly juxtaposed with his actual past i.e. his life outside the camera. he had cheated on his then-wife and attempted suicide. his daughter was in rehab for drugs usage and he was an emotionally unavailble, detached father all throughout

riggan chases this "better" artistic expression than superhero movies [which he despises greatly despite these same superhero movies being his biggest acheivement so far. his making of the play and executing it on broadway is his way of redeeming himself as an artist - trying to please the intellectual crowd - trying to prove himself worthy of proper critical acclaim and not just horde of fans

as riggan walks amongst crowds of fans screaming his name, he is turned off and annoyed. while, he wants to chase that one lone critic at the bar to hopefully sway her in his favor. he loathes his past because it was that same generic bullshit remade everytime; explosions, action, cgi. the same thing churned out everytime, the same thing expected everytime

and as he finally proves himself critically on broadway, proving himself to be worthy of being called an artist - reality strikes - he has to continue churning out the same play day in and day out since this play was such a hit. this same play which he would have to remake everytime at different places

don is quintessential indian cinema made with incredible care despite targeting the masses

the direction and writing is very much interested in making sure every part of the movie is coherent together but above that, that it is entertaining

the camera work is incredible at times and there are some unconventional handheld shots, low angle shots that are a delight to see

the legendary background ost which has been rehashed for decades still remains as thrilling as ever

all the musicals in between are all so well integrated into the movie and plot that future movies should also take note. instead of forcibly transitioning into a musical number, the plot so gradually leads into each one of the musical performances. and every song is such a banger

usually with indian masala flicks, the action doesnt age all too well but the action set pieces are so well choreographed that they age like fine wine here - they are just as fun and exciting even decades later

despite dealing with a serious plot regarding some great writing based on identities and criminals - the movie still retains an air of self awareness where even during the biggest climactic action set pieces, it doesnt take itself too seriously while still not making a mockery of itself, its delightful

amitabh bachchan is just a sight to behold - the absolute charm that comes over the screen as soon as he steps is like no other. he is so effortlessly able to switch between personas too, he is his usual self, super talented and charming

zeenat ji is such a delight to watch as usual. i was able to watch this movie at a screening where zeenat ji was present herself and its so surreal to see her 50 years later still as elegant

tldr
a great movie that transcended the conventions of indian masala flicks to deliver a strong story with some great acting performances

indian cinema is so back and its never been over

jawan is such a energetic, stylish, over-the-top, action-filled, humor filled blockbuster and if you dont atleast get a little excited while watching it, there's definitely something wrong with you

atlee has successfully brought srk back into form successfuly and with dunki to be released soon, we are so back

the film has a lot of style and its so fun to watch it unravel

more than that, this movie's foundation of being anti establishment resonates harder with the people its aimed at - the regular people and especially those who are wronged daily by the establishment

some scenes just straight up go so hard that it's honestly absurd; no action flick in my recent memory have went this hard. and all of them remain so stylish, straight from the first scene

there's some genuine sad story beats too which hit so well and would leave you sad

there are a few references to bollywood movies, some cameos, a shining reference, a matrix reference, a lion king reference - it has everything and its oh so fun

i went to watch this film at gaeity galaxy [an old theatre known for being the center of celebrations for such salman, shahrukh films] with my friend and i would not recommend any other experience for it. people losing their shit, clapping, cheering after a greedy capitalist selfish pig gets killed is an experience like none other

people would have cheered for srk regardless but atlee making it against the backdrop of the corrupt establishment is so raw and powerful man

the guy sitting next to me in the theatre was probably not as well to do as us and seeing him weep at the scenes of farmers being mistreated broke my heart because as much as we pose and pretend to care and have empathy - he probably lives through shit like loan sharks, bribing officials and so on. this dude who was drinking alcohol mid movie is the one who this movie affects the most as for a lot of privileged people like us will applaud, have fun and comment on the stylistic elements or blah blah cinematography, these movies provide the escapism - seeing greater than life characters makes them forget some of the horrible shit they go through every day

veer zaara is the pinnacle of the indian masala genre and explodes in a beautiful way helmed by veteran yash chopra and written by prodigal aditya chopra

its a love story which you once start believing will leave you in stiches

shahrukh is as good as he is

zinta also does some heavy work, Rani is also incredible

apart from the beautifully designed sets, camera work, immaculate dialogue, brilliant transitions and editing, elaborate dance pieces - the movie has aged so gracefully
the movie is about women empowerment a moment and then about pakistan-india relations where surprisingly for indian cinema, pakistan is not some evil entity existing to just cause pain to humanity but rather people just like us

even the main villain of the story is presented in a way where we could sympathize with them. the main fucking villain from pakistan is not villanized and is rather a product or unfortunate circumstances of having to forcibly marry under larger political bearings

incredible work from everyone, great movie

8 and a half is an execellent film crafted with multiple layers which would probably become much clearer to me on several rewatches

as is, the movie has a lot to say and decides to not say any of it but rather show all of it

owing to the surrealism fellini is known for, every internal and external conflict, every nuance is beautifully depicted with surreal imagery and out worldly sequencing

the meta-fiction layer being the most interesting

the director who's journey we are on as he is planning to make a film is able to encapsulate so much of "a man's" thought process that it's incredible

the intended symbolism might vary greatly from my interpretation of it but that's the fun of such movies! you get to gauge your own meanings from an abstract surreal piece

having dabbled in some amateur filmmaking myself since as long as i can remember; whether stupid home videos to youtube videos to some short films; the visualization and the sheer averse nature of the director's to actually tell people what the movie is about or rather get started with the filmmaking is one of the most striking things to me

further, the fact that his film is self-referential to the point where he could end up hurting the people in his life as he often tends to portray his real life experiences is very fascinating and something i am usually careful about when it comes to writing

i have always made a joke amongst my friends that everything that I write is always borrowed from the people around me and similarly, our protaganist finds himself in the same situation

the man wanting to delay the film as much as possible striving to reach that point of validation from the critic he despises while ignoring the people cheering him would have hit 3 years younger satyam so hard

the film also manifests in a meta-fictional layer with itself, where fellini often speaks to the people who watch his movie

guido wanting the critic to analyze his film; written by fellini himself being critical of his own film, the film being the one we are watching right now, being made

"i am sure you see the confusion and ambiguity"

"how can you not care if audiences dont understand"

another manifestation i really liked was the man's dream world being fulfiled where every woman he has ever been involved with or even has had any ilk of attaraction towards are all in one big harem coddling him and praising every word he says. where, even the bare minimum is to praised, even he is upset or overreacting is to be worshipped. a man's mind and fantasies truly manifests in digusting ways

every actor also does a fantastic job and the last 45 minutes of the film are near perfection

reviews.film: Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani
reviews.review:
rocky aur rani ki prem kahani is an excellent musical carried by incredible writing, performances and wonderful set designs

going into this, me and my friend expected an entertaining but an unimpactful bollywood masala where we would make fun of the melodrama and enjoy the experience as a whole but oh boy we were so wrong

everything about this movie from the dialogues to camera work to the musical numbers are handled with the utmost attention to detail

the first half of the movie leans heavily on the entertainment and humor surrounding the peculiar situation of their unlikely bond and wow the execution is so good. every joke lands and ranveer delivers an amazing performance as a loud delhi guy

each set and each location have a meticulous care given to it, and would rival wes anderson's frivolous hollow sets any day

the movie has a ton of heart and a lot of Bollywood homages too

a lot of old bollywood songs are also reused in such a beautiful way that you truly have nothing to complain about. theres a charulata song too!

the social messaging and the values it preaches are also so natural, geniune and progressive that i am honestly struck and dumbfounded

ranveer singh is a great fucking actor and this movie solidified it even further for me. alia bhatt is on top of her game. Jaya Bachchan is amazing, so is Dharmendra and everyone else in the film

every song, every word, every dialogue will have you in stiches and if youre a bollywood fan, you will cry (i did)

the second half picks up the pace and heightens the tension and the drama in such a great way oh my god, i couldnt breathe for a stretch of a 30 minutes

there are some great elongated one take shots too which is super commendable and wasnt necessary to be done

such a great film that as the credits roll down, and the film shows several scenes, those scenes are just as endearing and enticing as the entire movie

what a great time to be a bollywood fan, thank you karan johar
