this movie is so utterly personal to me, despite its flaws, has so many personal undertones to me. that being said, it might not be for everyone. the movie is more concerned with spirituality than any quantifiable entertainment so if that sounds like something exciting to you, then go watch it. if that doesn't excite you, don't watch it. but if you have watched it already, or dont plan to watch, you can read the below things

the unknown craftsman is a movie that I don't know where to begin, but I will start with a review that someone else wrote "praying via cinema" and I think that best describes this movie. this movie is indeed the process of praying through cinema. it's a thoroughly spiritual film and not even for a second does amit dutta have any intentions other than to pray and be spiritual

one of the thing that fascinates me the most is how through such careful shot composition, music selection, pacing; he is somehow able to pass on that spirutual and self-actualization who will be passively watching the movie. the film is surreal in its own right and basks in the surreality. the surreal nature of this film doesn't alienate in anyway but in a lynch-like swiftness, excites, allures and is cathartic

making sculptures or any art for that matter is treated as an act of spirituality (and rightfully so)

like previously mentioned, if a spiritual exploration through a film doesn't sound exciting, this is probably not the movie for you. and it doesnt particularly excite me either but man one thing got me through everything. lets talk about it last

the actors do a great job and the narrator is also incredible

some of the shots were so picturesque that I actually took some screenshots and really its a shame that this movie is not available in a good quality pretty much anywhere

okay so lastly, let's talk about himachal

the entire movie is set in himachal and it makes everything so personal and incredible

firstly, the locations are so incredible and so pretty, it made me revisit my childhood

and mainly, the elements resonated so deeply with me that I dont think any movie ever has

in between this movie, there is a personification of the local god, who guides our craftsman through his journey through a treacherous unmarked forest, and the god does it with so much ease; there has always been a saying in my village and one that my mom has always told me and that has been "raaste te khodo no mu, muh chaalu dui kadam aagde" which has brought me incredible comfort throughout my life and still continues to do when I am faced with regular life challenges. seeing it personified and realized on a screen was very special

the entire narration is done in pahadi too (even though the kangri dialect, i use the kullvi dialect), it fits the philosphical and spiritual tone of the movie so well

the melody that plays in the background is so instantly recognizable and reminds me of "हुरूआ बजुरूआ roti daahe tu chaane, aapu naye tu nahunda dhounda, baaye ka shuko paani" which is a local folk song of my village

before he uses a tree as a material, he prays to the tree and every entity surrounding it, which I have been taught since my childhood to do and continue to say everytime I eat or drink outside "jokhe laage teu khao jokhe na laye teu du mu doti beyi dhup paachi"

everything from "baajo lago na bojdo, lago no guide kordo" to the entire journey he had, resonated so much with me

i might not watch this movie very often and this is not that entertaining either but the transcendence of cinema as an artform of entertainment that this movie does is incredible.

even considering everything and all my personal biases, i would have given it 4 stars, but i still would rate it a 5 because if even one person amongst my friends gets pushed to watch this and has any small resemblance of any actualization inside of them, that's incredible to me

i didn't purposefully translate some of the pahari words i used above because they are personal to me and that's what I want. me writing this review is my way of completing the catharsis i had watching the movie

kathal is a fresh air of cinema amongst the thousands of lousy, insincere productions that plague all mainstream production houses

kathal is a social satire, love story, kidnapping mystery masquerading as an offbeat, silly movie

i dont even know where to begin because there is so much love put into every frame of this movie so I will start at the beginning: the kathals

two kathals of uncle hong variety are stolen from an MLA's house and that leads into an investigation from the police

the plot alone is silly enough to be interesting and make an entertaining movie and the movie does not do just that but rather goes the extra fucking mile

lets start with the social satire, the entire thing has countless moments of brilliance when it decides to satirically show contemporary evils plaguing our society yet it never for a second falls into the trap of ayushman khurannaesque profound monologues about “this evil thing that people do is actually bad wow” but rather tries to critique them by showing a sincere realistic depiction of the same [albeit through the eyes of our morally good protagonist]; this small choice lends so much authenticity to the movie and makes me want to appreciate it so much more

from the mla family spraying gangajal around the house just because a “lower” caste police officer has entered the house [which is a one second dialogue btw] to the default response of the mali being to sit on the floor when being asked to sit, its gut wrenchingly sad and thats a lot to say in such a silly, fun, offbeat movie

the movie also touches on worker exploitation in the same way, where the house-help tells the police of her “loyalty” to the MLA family by stating that she has once put her hand down the toilet just to retrieve some jewelry to Pateria beating the poor gardener up at the whim of his child

i have a lot of thoughts on this so please bear with me, this is going to be a long one

if you haven't watched it, i would say don't read the review further so as to not influence your interpretation because its a conceptual film that revels in unique interpretations

that being said, let's talk about the movie

there are disjointed thoughts on the various aspects throughout the film so i will try to divide them into "layers", starting from less significant to more

layer 1: absurd social satire

the movie has quite a few satirical pieces poking at the zeitgeist. some notable ones are: gentrification; when beau is walking across his street initially, we see a bunch of suited up men being scared by the mere presence of a homeless man and running away. immigration; when we are in that "children book storytelling/threatre" section (which is very pretty btw), the story resembles the stories of immigrants. from them being happy in their own home to their home being absolutely destroyed forcing them to move out where noone speaks their language and hence they get villainized and in turn all their hardships and problems are blamed on that person who looks different; loved this entire sequence. theres also reference to how severely medicated people are, to the point of a random child eating pills like snacks. and a panicky cop about to shoot an innocent man

layer 2: beau

when the movie first started, i was put off by some sequences and felt that aster was being weird for the sake of it but then it clicked, beau is a child and that gets clear as we move further in the story. beau might have a body of an adult but he is indeed still a child and there's a small funny joke/nod to it too; when elaine meets beau after so long, she says:
"you're the same except your body and the face"

once we understand this about beau, a lot of the movie clicks for us and the overly exaggerated visuals make sense because its a child going through it

when i say beau is a child, i obviously dont want to take away from the nuances behind the character, theres depth to how and why the character is what it is and its phoenix's incredible acting that sells it. from his diction to the subtle mannerisms, its incredible what aster and phoenix are able to achieve and convey without for a moment being cringe worthy

beau is a deeply disturbed person who went through a lot of trauma as a child and suppressing and accepting it all his life has caused him to never really being able to escape that childlike thinking and remains in perpetual servitude towards his mom

his mother has always consistently harmed him and made him walk on eggshells that even after him being old, a single phone call has him down on his knees making sure his mom is feeling absolutely fine and trying to interpret the silences in a phone conversation and how what her mom is saying is obviously not what she means

the mother is deeply disturbed and lacked a loving family as a child and hence overcompensates it towards her children and when they dont reciprocate it in the exact same manner in the exact same way that she wants, she snaps and wishes they would die instead and grows resentful

the mother being a single mom has pressure added and fails even more at parenting, the mother since beau's birth has controlled every aspect of his life and lied to him just so she can have even more control and prevent what she considers "bad" for him and this continues into his adulthood

she has cameras all over his house, drugs him with a fake medicine, will scream at him, terrifies him of ever having sex because of a "genetic disease", terrifies him of eating anything sweet, gets angry when he falls in love for the first time because it would take away from him giving priority to her and her alone. she also kills the woman he first has sex with, and the househelp who beau really liked and was bonding with. just so beau loved her and her alone

she seperates the boy from his father which i speculate is because she didnt want to "share" the child. locks away his twin brother when he asks questions about his father, all the while painting the father as a horrible monster, so much so that beau [being a child] visualizes him as a disgusting physical monster (eraser head baby as an adult lol?)

beau is consistently used by various "adults" to project their own needs and wants onto him. he is hit by a couple who take him in and try to make him his son, who is a replacement for their son who probably died in the army

multiple adults keep forcing him into decisions but in the end framing it along the lines of "oh if you say so"

beau, tragically, ends up being a child being used by all the supposed adults as he clutches onto his toy (virgin mary) and shares it with the one woman who he is nice to him when he needs help

layer 3: meta commentary / us

the one thing that movie does so fucking well is blurring the line between fiction and reality

aster at times combines a lot of elements of his previous works into this film, which somehow feel like a self-aware harmless parody

but it goes deeper than that, a lot of the times the movie focuses shift onto someone very important to the movie, us

the movie shifts its crosshair towards the audience a lot through various techniques and questions our morals and stances

there are two ways it does this, lets discuss the first one

there are various times where the editing/pacing are deliberately shown in ways where in movies usually a joke precedes (an execution of a joke) but the actual setup isnt there and is usually something very horrific and leaves us to do some introspection

from beau hitting his head, to almost getting shot by a panicky cop, to someone being stabbed and gasping; these are all edited/presented in a very marvel esque joke setup ways and the people in my theatre did laugh but that makes us people revelling and enjoying a person being hurt, even though fictional, but a person none the less. the juxtaposition of humor and horrific is a good way to critique us

this critique of us is full blown and in center where when beau is on the most horrific situation, on a boat and his whole life is being recounted and his trauma being relived, we alike the audience sitting in the movie, eat our popcorns and discuss it, like we do for a lot of horrific things we hear about in our daily lives and when its all over, and the credits roll, we alike the audience in the movie get up and leave because hey fun movie innit, lets write a big ass letterboxd review now

lets discuss the other way now,
ari aster, similar to many other directors, often uses trauma as the centerpiece of his movies and explores it in various ways. and even without trauma, various movies work because we start empathizing with the characters and seeing ourselves in them. like previously mentioned, the meta commentary continues with beau watching the moving theatre performance being a surrogate for us watching aster's movies and seeing ourselves in it. the entire sequence parallels how us the audience would interact with aster's work (or movies in general) and at times end up with a cathartic outlet and even though maybe exaggerate the fiction by relating to it too much (as is seen when the theatre performance shifts to a low production play when beau snaps back to reality)

beau screaming "this is my story", "this is me" is us going "literally me"

conclusion:

all in all, beau is afraid is a lynchian conceptual film where trauma and its effects are explored once again with a very impressive cast, pretty visualizations and an overall crisp runtime despite touching on so much

i am just an idiot who is looking too much into it and aster just wanted to be quirky and weird :p
